models.author: ARSH VERMA
models.description:
Model Summary

CodeLens-Reviewer is an AI agent fine-tuned to act as a Senior Code Reviewer. Built upon the Qwen2.5-Coder architecture, this model has been instruction-tuned by Arsh Verma to autonomously detect bugs, identify security vulnerabilities, and critique architectural flaws in Python Pull Requests. It interacts directly with the CodeLens Evaluation Environment, outputting perfectly structured JSON actions to simulate an automated code review loop.

Usage

This model is intended to be used either standalone for code inference or plugged into the live CodeLens Evaluation Environment. You can load it using the FastLanguageModel from Unsloth in 4-bit precision.

Shape of Inputs/Outputs:
- Input: Natural language instructions and a python code snippet.
- Output: A strict JSON object containing action, issue_description, filename, line_number, severity, and category.

Known Failures: The model may hallucinate specific line numbers if the provided code diff is extremely long or poorly formatted.

System

This model serves as the core Agent in the CodeLens Evaluation System. It receives system prompts, noise budgets, and task definitions from the CodeLens Python backend. Its downstream dependency is the CodeLens WebSocket dashboard, which parses the JSON outputs to assign rewards and update the live leaderboard.

Implementation requirements

- Hardware: Trained on a single NVIDIA Tesla T4 x2 GPU via Kaggle.
- Software: Unsloth, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, TRL.
- Compute: Fine-tuning took less than 15 minutes due to Unsloth highly optimized 4-bit LoRA training pipeline. Inference requires under 6GB of VRAM, making it incredibly lightweight and accessible.

Model Characteristics

The model was fine-tuned from the pre-trained unsloth/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct base model. It contains 7 Billion Parameters. LoRA adapters were applied to Q, K, V, O, gate, up, and down projections. The model was trained and quantized in 4-bit to severely reduce VRAM requirements.

Data Overview

The model was trained on a highly specific, synthetically generated instructional dataset targeting code review tasks.

The training data contains custom prompt-completion pairs. Each row simulates a CodeLens environment state containing a PR title, a code diff containing planted bugs, and a golden JSON completion representing the ideal code review action.

Evaluation Results

The model successfully learned the JSON formatting constraints and correctly identifies logic bugs (e.g., modifying arrays during iteration) without hallucinating markdown wrappers.

- Bug Detection: High accuracy. Successfully identifies off-by-one and logical loop errors.
- Security Audit: Capable of identifying basic input sanitization failures.
- Architecture: Demonstrates baseline capability in flagging Single Responsibility Principle violations.

This model is intended strictly for evaluating code within isolated sandboxes or assisting developers. It should not be used to automatically reject or approve production Pull Requests without human oversight, as false positives are possible. No sensitive or PII data was used during the training of this model.

instances.overview: Rank 16 LoRA adapters fine-tuned on the Qwen2.5-Coder 7B architecture using Unsloth. Trained specifically for the CodeLens evaluation environment to output structured JSON for bug detection.
instances.usage:
from unsloth import FastLanguageModel

# 1. Load the CodeLens Model
model, tokenizer = FastLanguageModel.from_pretrained(
    model_name = "ArshVerma/CodeLens-Reviewer", 
    max_seq_length = 2048,
    load_in_4bit = True,
)
FastLanguageModel.for_inference(model)

# 2. Provide a code snippet with a bug
prompt = "You are an expert code reviewer. Review the following code and output a JSON action indicating any bugs or issues you find.\n\nCode:\ndef process(data):\n    for i in data:\n        if i == 'remove': data.remove(i)\n    return data"

messages = [
    {"role": "system", "content": "You are an expert code reviewer. Output only valid JSON."},
    {"role": "user", "content": prompt}
]

inputs = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
    messages, 
    tokenize=True, 
    add_generation_prompt=True, 
    return_tensors="pt"
).to("cuda")

# 3. Generate the AI Code Review
outputs = model.generate(input_ids=inputs, max_new_tokens=256)
print(tokenizer.batch_decode(outputs)[0])

instances.overview:
# Depth-dependent synthetic-fog NAFNet

Experimental post-submission extension to the computational defogging project. This checkpoint starts from the paired fog-chamber NAFNet and is further trained for one epoch, capped at 2,600 optimizer updates, using synthetic fog whose attenuation is modulated by precomputed ZoeDepth maps.

This model is not part of the final PNAS submission. Generator-specific synthetic metrics should not be interpreted as real-fog benchmark results. The checkpoint also showed severe color clipping on five of six audited raw aircraft frames and is released for reproducibility rather than as the recommended default.

Code, results, and the paper variant are documented at https://github.com/theMenonlab/defogging/tree/main/experiments/depth_dependent_fog.
instances.usage:
# Model format

PyTorch NAFNet state dictionary with compact embedded provenance. The required output wrapper is `residual_rgb`.

# Inputs and outputs

Input: RGB image tensor normalized to `[0, 1]`.

Output: defogged RGB image. Use the included tiled inference runner and matching JSON config.

# Inference

```bash
python run_defogging_inference.py \
  --checkpoint nafnet_depth_dependent_synthetic_20260722.pth \
  --model-config run_config_depth_dependent_synthetic_nafnet.json \
  --input /path/to/foggy_images \
  --output-dir outputs/depth_dependent \
  --tile-size 512 \
  --tile-overlap 64 \
  --save-comparison
```

Verify the downloaded checkpoint with `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt`.

instances.overview:
# Mixed chamber and synthetic training NAFNet

Experimental post-submission extension to the computational defogging project. This NAFNet is trained from fresh initialization while deterministically interleaving 247,150 paired fog-chamber updates with 2,600 randomized-synthetic Mapillary updates. The schedule matches the synthetic-update budget of the earlier sequential experiment.

This model is not part of the final PNAS submission. The 0.2x and 5x schedules are sensitivity experiments; this release contains the matched-budget current-ratio checkpoint.

Code, results, and the paper variant are documented at https://github.com/theMenonlab/defogging/tree/main/experiments/mixed_chamber_synthetic_training.

models.author: Alexey Kabanov
models.description:
# Customer Churn Sklearn Baseline

This is an educational scikit-learn baseline model for binary customer churn classification.

## Intended use

This model is intended for beginner-friendly machine learning practice on Kaggle. It demonstrates a simple, reproducible workflow for training and saving a tabular classification model.

The model should be used for learning purposes only.

## Task

The task is binary classification.

The target column is:

- `churn`

Target meaning:

- `1` — the synthetic customer churned;
- `0` — the synthetic customer was retained.

## Training data

The model was trained on the Synthetic Customer Churn Starter Dataset.

The dataset is fully synthetic. It does not contain real customer records, personal data, real transactions, or real company data.

## Model architecture

The model is a scikit-learn `Pipeline` with:

- median imputation for numeric features;
- most-frequent imputation for categorical features;
- one-hot encoding for categorical features;
- `RandomForestClassifier` for prediction.

## Input features

Numeric features:

- `age`
- `tenure_months`
- `monthly_charges`
- `support_tickets`

Categorical features:

- `contract_type`
- `internet_service`

## Output

The model predicts customer churn as a binary class.

Depending on how it is loaded, the pipeline can also be used to produce churn probabilities with `predict_proba`.

## Validation

The model was evaluated with 5-fold stratified cross-validation.

The validation metric is accuracy.

## Files

- `customer_churn_sklearn_pipeline.joblib` — trained scikit-learn pipeline.
- `feature_schema.json` — feature and target schema.
- `sample_input.csv` — example input rows.
- `model_metrics.json` — validation metrics and metadata.
- `requirements.txt` — minimal Python dependencies.
- `README.md` — model card and usage documentation.

## Limitations

This is a simple educational baseline, not a production model.

The training data is synthetic, so the model should not be used for real customer churn decisions or business automation.

The dataset is intentionally small and simplified, so model performance should not be interpreted as real-world churn prediction performance.

## License

CC0 1.0 Universal.

# Random Forest Baseline

This model instance contains a scikit-learn RandomForest baseline for synthetic customer churn classification.

The model is packaged as a scikit-learn Pipeline. It includes preprocessing steps and the classifier in one reusable object.

## Task

Binary classification.

Target:

- `churn`

Target values:

- `1` — customer churned;
- `0` — customer was retained.

## Framework

scikit-learn

## Files

- `customer_churn_sklearn_pipeline.joblib` — trained scikit-learn Pipeline.
- `feature_schema.json` — feature and target schema.
- `sample_input.csv` — example input rows.
- `model_metrics.json` — validation metrics and metadata.
- `requirements.txt` — minimal dependencies.
- `README.md` — model card documentation.

## Intended use

This model instance is intended for Kaggle learning, baseline modeling, and demonstration of the Kaggle Models workflow.

It should not be used for real customer churn decisions because the training data is fully synthetic.
instances.usage:
from pathlib import Path

import joblib
import pandas as pd


# Find model files inside Kaggle input folders
input_root = Path("/kaggle/input")

model_files = sorted(input_root.rglob("customer_churn_sklearn_pipeline.joblib"))
sample_files = sorted(input_root.rglob("sample_input.csv"))

if not model_files:
    raise FileNotFoundError("Could not find customer_churn_sklearn_pipeline.joblib")

model_path = model_files[0]
print(f"Loading model from: {model_path}")

model = joblib.load(model_path)


# Load sample input if available
if sample_files:
    sample_input = pd.read_csv(sample_files[0])
else:
    sample_input = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "age": [35, 52],
            "tenure_months": [12, 48],
            "monthly_charges": [89.9, 54.5],
            "support_tickets": [4, 1],
            "contract_type": ["month-to-month", "two-year"],
            "internet_service": ["fiber", "dsl"],
        }
    )


predictions = model.predict(sample_input)

result = sample_input.copy()
result["predicted_churn"] = predictions

if hasattr(model, "predict_proba"):
    result["churn_probability"] = model.predict_proba(sample_input)[:, 1]

result

models.description: SysTools [MBOX Email Address Extractor Tool](https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9nd2qdjst1kv) is a specialized utility designed to extract email addresses from MBOX mailbox files quickly and accurately. The software scans MBOX files and retrieves email addresses from various email fields, including To, From, CC, BCC, and Reply-To, helping users build comprehensive email address lists from mailbox data. The tool supports MBOX files created by popular email clients such as Thunderbird, Apple Mail, Eudora, Entourage, SeaMonkey, Spicebird, and other MBOX-supported applications. Users can process multiple MBOX files simultaneously, making it suitable for organizations, marketing teams, investigators, and professionals who need to collect email addresses from large mailbox archives. The software provides advanced filtering options that allow users to extract specific email addresses based on their requirements. Extracted email IDs can be saved in commonly used formats for future reference and analysis. Throughout the extraction process, the tool maintains data accuracy and ensures that the original mailbox files remain unchanged. With its simple interface and straightforward workflow, SysTools MBOX Email Address Extractor can be used by both technical and non-technical users. The software performs all operations locally, ensuring complete privacy and security of mailbox data. Key Features: - Extract email addresses from MBOX mailbox files. - Retrieve email IDs from To, From, CC, BCC, and Reply-To fields. - Support Thunderbird, Apple Mail, Eudora, Entourage, and other MBOX-based email clients. - Process multiple MBOX files in batch mode. - Extract email addresses from selected mailbox folders. - Apply filters to refine extraction results. - Save extracted email addresses for future use. - Maintain data accuracy throughout the extraction process. - Preserve original MBOX files without modification. - User-friendly interface suitable for all types of users.
